R3-01.why: Best hook-to-thumbnail of the set: 'party, then hide the evidence before Mom gets home' is instantly relatable to kids and teens, YouTuber-friendly (FREEZE catches, snitch betrayals, Report Card punchlines), and rides the asymmetric 1vN lineage that has had long tails on Roblox (Flee the Facility, Granny-likes) plus the Oct 2026 Next Fest asymmetric-comedy signal. The only cited competitor (Clean the House!, ~5-8K peak) is PvE, so the theme is open. Monetization is the strongest here: the Parent is the most-watched character every round (costumes, car skins seen by everyone in the cutscene), Report Card poses and emotes get screen time every round, and the giftable lobby Bedroom adds a social space and a reason to come back. 5-7 player servers fill reasonably for 1vN. It is cosmetic-only, so FTC and dark-pattern exposure is low. The drags are scope and live-ops cost. Four distinct phases including a separate driving mini-game, ~25 stateful evidence objects and 60 hiding spots per house, gadgets, decoys and snitching are a lot for 2-5 devs in 3-4 months. Each new house is expensive content (spot curation, balance), so a monthly house cadence is costly. The Parent's 1:45 solo drive also takes one player out of the shared chaos at the most social moment.
R3-01.fix: Biggest commercial risk is scope/live-ops cost versus a 28-day retention window: if launch slips or houses come slowly, retention signals never mature. Cut the driving mini-game to a simple 'stall Mom' meter (or ship it post-launch), launch with 1 house plus mutators, and make House Rule mutators and kid/Parent loadouts carry weeks 1-8 so new houses are not the only retention lever. Also watch Parent-role demand imbalance (queue preference/tickets earned by playing kid).

R3-02.why: Fresh input hook that plays to mobile touch, solo-playable 1-4 co-op (good for cold start), and a roguelite relic draft that can drive 28-day retention. The investment case is weak on demand evidence: the nearest analogue, Draw Spells Magic Arena, sits around ~615 CCU, which suggests 'draw to cast' alone does not pull a Roblox audience. Co-op wave defence competes with entrenched tower-defence giants on a very different, more idle-friendly loop. Fusion needs two players casting within 1 s, which works with voice-chatting friends but rarely with silent randoms, so the headline feature is weakest exactly in matchmade play. Console and PC inputs are second-class. Server-side gesture classification adds latency risk to the core feel. Monetization surfaces (ink trails, familiars, finishers) are visible but lower status than avatar-level or role-level cosmetics. Displaying players' drawn traces 'big on screen for viewers' risks reading as free-form drawing under Kids/Select rules, which would lock out the under-16 audience. Live-ops are moderate: new runes ripple through every fusion and enemy-counter combination.
R3-02.fix: Biggest commercial risk is low proven demand plus a Kids/Select gating problem. Never show raw player strokes to others (show only the canonical classified glyph), and make fusion trigger reliably with randoms (e.g., widen the window, auto-suggest and snap partner casts). Validate with a cheap prototype soft-launch before committing: if D1 is under ~20%, kill it.

R3-03.why: Very legible, cheap-to-build concept: one rule ('let go = freeze, only the beam can tag you') that a kid gets from a thumbnail, with Red-Light-Green-Light and Night-at-the-Museum framing that has broad cross-age appeal. Lowest production risk of the asymmetric pair (one museum, humanoid R15 statues, 8 pranks), and live-ops are cheap: new prank sets and Exhibit events are mostly scripting plus props, and wings are reusable. Monetization is solid: disguise-pack statue skins are credited by name at the Unmasking, and Guard beam/tag effects are the most visible items in the game. It is release-to-freeze native to mobile. Skeptical points: hide-in-plain-sight is a crowded Roblox niche (Be NPC or Die, DISGUISE, In Plain Sight) where games tend to spike and fade because the core gets solved. Watching a flashlight and holding still has less escalation and fewer shareable moments than GROUNDED's chaos, and fewer meta hooks for a 28-day signal. Lag-judged freezing on mobile networks is a fairness and complaint risk that hurts reviews and retention. The ceiling looks like a solid mid-tier hit rather than a breakout.
R3-03.fix: Biggest commercial risk is shallow mastery leading to a 2-3 week decay curve in a crowded hide-in-plain-sight niche. Front-load depth that the Guard and statues can both master (rotating hidden pranks, statue abilities, Guard gadgets, ranked Guard ladder at launch, not later), and budget a weekly Exhibit cadence from day one so the 28-day window sees fresh content.

R3-04.why: The strongest co-play and invite engine on paper: the game literally needs friends in seats, which feeds Roblox's co-play signal. The Captain rule plus 'chip in' gifting is a smart social monetization loop, and vehicles directly buyable alongside earnable ones scale with cadence. It is the easiest build of the five (kinematic spline raft, one HOLD button, auto camera), ideal for a small team and fully mobile-native. Sports & Racing was one of the few growing categories. The demand evidence is thin or fad-shaped, though. Boat Together's ~2K all-time peak is the closest direct analogue, and the Fart Together spike was crude-humor virality that got taken down, not proof of retention. 'Together' co-op novelty games typically spike and decay inside the 28-day window. Matchmade randoms coordinating paddles is weaker fun than friends, so cold start for solo joiners is a concern. Live-ops cost is moderate (a vehicle every 2-3 weeks with unique seat roles needs balancing).
R3-04.fix: Biggest commercial risk is novelty decay: it is fun for three sessions, then gone before 28-day signals mature. Ship the retention spine at launch: daily-seed crew leaderboard, segment medals, Versus, and a crew/Boathouse progression. Add AI/bot seat fill so 1-2 players can start immediately, and keep humor strictly kid-safe to avoid the takedown pattern that hit its inspiration.

R3-05.why: The best long-term retention architecture in the set. A creature collection with performance-gated rares (earned, never sold) is the proven Roblox return-visit engine (pet-collection lineage; Rescue Animals ~20K peak shows the animal-rescue theme pulls), and companions follow you in the lobby and ride your truck in runs (visible to everyone), which drives both status and invites. Firefighters plus animals is evergreen, broad, safe, Kids/Select-friendly and low moderation risk. Solo-playable 1-4 co-op solves cold start better than the asymmetric concepts, and 'drag a friend out of the smoke' gives natural co-play moments. Monetization is diversified (companion accessories, hose effects on screen constantly, liveries via Captain rule, giftables, companion slots). Skeptical points: the audience skews young, where Roblox is cutting impressions for short-term-monetized games and where the 18+ DevEx bonus barely applies, so ARPU per DAU will trail teen/adult concepts. Refusing paid critters leaves the genre's biggest revenue lever on the table (correct for regulation, but it caps upside). Content cost is the highest of the five: fire grid, hose feel, critter AI behaviours, procedural rooms, 20-40 critters at launch, plus 10 critters and a new building type each season. Overcooked-style co-op chaos has historically been mid-tier on Roblox.
R3-05.fix: Biggest commercial risk is content burn: the collection loop only retains if critters arrive faster than players finish the log, and each building type is expensive. Build a critter pipeline (2 rigs, variant-driven: colour, accessory and behaviour presets) so +10 critters is a weekly-ish asset task, not a sprint. Gate rares across alarm tiers so one building type sustains 6-8 weeks, and push the teen/adult hook (ranked alarm-5 speedruns) to lift ARPU.

overall_notes: Skeptical-investor ranking: R3-01 GROUNDED! (7) and R3-05 BLAZE BRIGADE (7) lead for different reasons. GROUNDED has the best virality and cosmetic visibility but the heaviest launch scope. BLAZE has the best 28-day retention spine and cold-start profile but the highest ongoing content cost and a younger, lower-ARPU audience. Tie-break: BLAZE if the team can industrialise critter production; GROUNDED if the team can cut the driving mini-game and still ship in ~4 months. R3-03 STATUE SHUFFLE (6) is the cheapest, safest asymmetric bet with a lower ceiling in a crowded niche. R3-04 PADDLE PANIC (6) is the easiest build with the strongest invite loop but has the weakest demand evidence and high novelty-decay risk. R3-02 SCRIBBLE SPELLS (5) has the least proven demand (closest analogue ~615 CCU), a fusion hook that degrades with randoms, and possible Kids/Select drawing-rule exposure. Macro context: DAU is down 9% YoY, discovery favours retention and older players, and under-16 reach costs a fee plus a 500-engaged-plays evaluation. Every concept should budget that gate into the launch plan and plan for a 28-day cold start with paid sponsorship or creator seeding, not organic hope. Confidence is medium throughout: tracker data is noisy and no concept has playtest metrics.
